acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

data.reason: Angela, the COO, signed with Adyen after they showed store rollout experience and one vendor for tills and web. Tom first named Raj as decider and credited our online strength, but stores decided it.

trigger.action: Lead with online orders returned at the store till.
trigger.why: Stores couldn't see online orders, and Angela reportedly watched the returns queue on December 27th.
trigger.quote: The store couldn't see the online order

decider.action: Speak to the COO's store worries: returns, tills, one vendor accountable.
decider.why: Angela signed with Adyen, but Tom pitched mostly to Raj, the CTO, and met her only once.

competitor.action: Say who runs store rollouts and installs, and name retailers.
competitor.why: Raj said Adyen brought a team with store rollout experience. This is secondhand. Afterwards 11 of 14 questions were about stores.

message.action: Replace the 'line has disappeared' claim with a step-by-step till return.
message.why: Bev called our unified commerce slide a diagram and asked how a return works at the till.

proof.action: Add a store retailer story with rollout dates and who installs.
proof.why: Angela asked to talk to the case study retailer, and we couldn't set up a call in time.

words.action: Say 'the tills' and 'one customer, one basket', not point of sale.
words.why: Bev and Angela never said unified commerce, while we kept saying in-person payments and point of sale.
words.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
